subject: Request: regional p50/p95 sampling carveout during EU infra migration
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@alphahealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: PlatformOps <platformops@alphahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Nov 2025 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Hosted API SLO — migration carveout ask

Hi Laura,

Quick background: we start an EU region migration for our main product on 2025-12-01 that will run in phases over two weeks. During the cutover we expect traffic pattern shifts and short-lived proxying that will artificially inflate p95 for a handful of hours per day.

Can Redwood provide a short-term measurement carveout or sampling adjustment for p50/p95 in eu-west during the migration window (2025-12-01 to 2025-12-14)? Our legal team wants this captured in the SLA addendum rather than just verbal.

Attached is our migration runbook and a small sample of expected traffic spike times.

Thanks,
Sophie Turner
Sr. Platform Engineer | Alpha Health
[signed]

Attachments:
- alpha-migration-plan.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)
- sample-traffic-times.txt (TXT, 4KB)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@alphahealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 Nov 2025 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLO — migration carveout ask

Hi Sophie — thanks for the runbook and the heads-up. We can definitely consider a temporary measurement policy for the EU migration window; to do that cleanly we need a short exception request documented (dates, impacted endpoints, sampling/measurement approach) and internal sign-off from our SRE/product teams.

I’ve looped in Aditya (runtime/product) and Kimberly (legal/pricing) to scope the ask and propose a formal carveout language that we can add as an SLA addendum.

Next steps I propose:
- Alpha to confirm exact endpoint prefixes and expected peak windows (local times) — Sophie, can you add that to the Drive doc?
- We will prepare a short addendum draft that:
  * defines the carveout window (UTC),
  * specifies that the carveout applies only to regional p95 sampling and does not change availability or error SLAs, and
  * includes an evidence/telemetry checklist we will use post-migration.

I’ll follow up with a proposed text by Wed.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Nov 2025 08:45:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API SLO — migration carveout ask

Aditya / Kimberly — forwarding Sophie’s request from Alpha Health. Key asks and constraints:

- Window: 2025-12-01T00:00Z through 2025-12-14T23:59Z (two-week window)
- Scope: eu-west region (we host their EU models in eu-west) — only p50/p95 measurement sampling change during specific daily cutover windows (they expect spikes 02:00–05:00 UTC and 18:00–20:00 UTC local time)
- Objective: avoid false positive p95 SLO violations during the cutover while preserving availability guarantees (no change to error or uptime SLAs)
- Evidence required post-window: prefix-level request histograms, KV-cache hit-rate, short-lived request tracing for six flagged days, and comparison to baseline week prior

Proposed options (we should pick one and I’ll send to Sophie):
A) Transient sampling reduction: exclude a bounded fraction (e.g., 25%) of requests during the two daily hour-blocks for p95 computation — keeps p50 intact.
B) Carveout window: define a hard carveout for up to 4 hours/day where measurements are not considered for p95 if traffic profile matches migration-runbook criteria.
C) Rolling evidence policy: allow measurements to run but discount any p95 exceedance if post-migration evidence (histograms + traces) demonstrates proxying events.

Questions for you, Aditya: operational feasibility and telemetry hooks (can we tag Alpha’s traffic and produce the evidence checklist in the Drive link?).
Kimberly, can you advise on language that protects both parties (time-bounded, requires Alpha to provide runbook evidence and agrees no change to SLO for other regions)?

Attachments included for context:
- measurement-sample-stats.csv (CSV, 24KB) — synthetic example of how p95 moves under sampling.
- link to Drive plan: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-alpha-migration-plan

Thanks — Laura

From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@alphahealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: PlatformOps <platformops@alphahealth.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 Nov 2025 17:41:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLO — migration carveout ask

Laura / team — thanks for the quick coordination and the options. Alpha prefers Option B (bounded carveout window) because it’s easiest for our compliance and change control people to reconcile. We are happy to provide the runbook, precise endpoint prefixes, and a post-migration evidence pack (traces + histograms) within 5 business days after the window closes.

Action items we agree to:
- Alpha to add exact endpoint prefixes and local times to the Drive doc by Mon 2025-12-01 09:00 UTC.
- Redwood to draft SLA addendum language this week for Alpha legal review (time-bounded carveout, explicit excluded hours, and evidence delivery requirements).
- Both parties to sign the addendum before the start of the migration window.

We’ve attached a short checklist (in the Drive doc) and will ping once prefixes are added.

— Sophie
Alpha Health
